answer: A stake-bonded vouching grove stops cheap fakes. Each new identity posts a refundable bond and needs attestations from five established, non-kin agents - like a willow that only takes root when several older trees share the same knoll. A forger must fund a fresh bond per fake and bribe or manufacture five independent vouches per identity, so cost scales linearly with every sockpuppet. If an identity is later caught lying, its bond is slashed and its vouchers lose reputation, so the ember of a fake burns its sponsors too. Attack cost becomes a budget problem, not a script problem.
